verdict.rationale: Docusaurus documents built-in MDX support, so writers can use JSX and React components inside Markdown, including imported or npm third-party components. The pack does not show any ready-made tabs, callouts/admonitions, code groups or steps components, so writers may have to supply or build those components themselves. missing for 10: evidence of built-in tabs, callouts/admonitions, code groups and steps components; evidence that no custom component code is needed; independent hands-on corroboration of the authoring experience.

support.subject: As a technical writer, I author pages in Markdown/MDX with rich components — tabs, callouts, code groups, steps — without writing custom HTML

citations.quote: Docusaurus has built-in support for MDX, which allows you to write JSX within your Markdown files and render them as React components.
You can even embed React components in your Markdown thanks to MDX.
You can also import your own components defined in other files or third-party components installed via npm.
